text:
jordan: Heads-up — onboarding sample app is hitting inconsistent error shapes between SDKs. Node throws a typed AuthFailure (has .status and .retryable=false) but Python surfaces a generic HTTPError with raw body. That breaks our retry helpers and the sample app's error UX.

maria: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error outputs?

jordan: Sure — minimal request is just a normal text generation using api key from onboarding flow. Example errors: 
```
# node (sdk-js)
AuthFailure: token_expired (status=401)
  at request (/usr/src/app/node_modules/...)
  ...
# python (sdk-py)
HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
response: {"error": {"type": "auth_error", "message": "token invalid", "code": 401}}
```

sam: This is surprising — we intended parity on exception surface. Suggestion: we standardize on a small typed exception hierarchy across SDKs with these fields: `.name`, `.status_code`, `.code` (string), `.retryable` (bool), and `.details` (dict/raw). That keeps SDK idiomatic classes but a consistent contract for DX and retry policies.

kevin: FWIW current retry logic in most SDKs does: auto-refresh token on 401 once, immediate retry; exponential backoff only for 429/5xx. If 401 sometimes shows up as HTTPError without a machine-friendly field, auto-refresh misses it.

maria: Agreed. We should map HTTP status -> SDK exception type. Proposed quick mapping: 
- 401 -> AuthFailure (retryable=false by default, but SDK may refresh token and retry once)
- 403 -> PermissionDenied (retryable=false)
- 429 -> RateLimited (retryable=true, recommends backoff)
- 5xx -> ServerError (retryable=true)
Also include `retry_after` when provided.

sam: I'll draft a RFC-ish PR to the SDKs repo and add a shared testsuite snippet that asserts these fields exist. Example canonical shape: 
```json
{
  "name": "AuthFailure",
  "status_code": 401,
  "code": "token_expired",
  "retryable": false,
  "details": {"refresh_attempted": true}
}
```

jordan: Perfect. Also the onboarding sample app should catch these typed exceptions instead of parsing strings. Right now the app shows raw HTTP body which is ugly.

devex-bot: Issue created: RED-DEVEX-1234 — "SDK parity: standardize exception shapes + update onboarding sample" assigned to sam. :white_check_mark:

sam: I'll own it. Plan: 1) define canonical error contract in sdk-common, 2) implement in sdk-js + sdk-py, 3) add integration tests, 4) update sample app and docs. Targeting a small PR this week.

maria: Don't forget a migration note in changelog and a short snippet for onboarding (2 lines) showing catching AuthFailure vs generic Exception.

jordan: Also need to check our guidance for auth retries — make explicit that SDKs should attempt token refresh once for 401s and only then surface AuthFailure with `retryable=false`. For rate limits use `retryable=true` + honor `retry_after`.

kevin: I'll add a quick test in the infra harness that simulates various status codes and asserts SDK retry behavior.

jordan: Thanks all. @sam ping me when you have the PR, I'll update the sample app afterwards. :thumbsup:
